about: The machine statement a CANOPY heartbeat carries beside the connector's identity, and what the viewer shows for it. `reachable` is {state: yes|no|unknown, since: epoch s|null, reason: sentence|null}; `writes` is {state: on|asked|off|locked|applying|held, reason: sentence|null, cause: the connector's cause id|null}; each is absent or null (no claim) or a complete object. Only `on` and `asked` accept writes: at `asked` the viewer opens its confirmation dialog before every write and sends each write with `confirmed: true`; `held` is inert, a watchdog's hold on the session, with the hold's reason as the hover and `writes held` on the badge. A word a reader does not know is inert. `legacy_frame` is a heartbeat with neither key. `reachable_frames` and `writes_frames` are single live frames; `summaries` are `/hare/v1/health/summary` bodies and the statement fields read from them. Every `expected` view gives the badge text and tone, whether write widgets are inert, their hover sentence (a null reason reads as the `Writes are off/locked/held for <label>` / `Applying the new write state for <label>` default) and the badge title's `since_text` while `reachable` is `no`. `since_text_cases`: the phrase for `since` and the frame's `timestamp`, the time of `since` in time zone `tz` as HH:MM (24-hour, seconds dropped) and the duration `timestamp - since` in whole minutes, rounded down. `sequences` are frame lists replayed in order on one page; `close` is a socket gap. Each step's `expected` holds the view after it and the toasts it raises (texts, in order); steps are further apart than the 10-s reachability toast limiter. `since_text` in frame cases and sequences is computed in UTC.

sequences.description: The machine stops answering; the backend restarts on the same binding and the successor carries the drop's `since`. No second outage toast.
An outage, a socket gap and an `unknown` frame, then `yes`: `unknown` and the gap neither toast nor reset the last definite state, so exactly one recovery toast.
An outage, the backend restarts on the same binding with the carried `since`, then the machine answers: one recovery toast.
Writes turned off: the outgoing backend's live frame says `off`, it restarts and the successor says `off` again. One writes toast, on the live frame.
